title: Physiological and environmental drivers of language change for the Mishkenaz premise and its Galut layers
question: Which empirically documented mechanisms - articulatory/phonetic sound change, areal and environmental influences on phonology, language contact, koineization, and diaspora/exile language evolution such as Yiddish, Ladino, and Judeo-Arabic or substrate effects in scattered communities - should ground the central premise that Mishkenaz changed through physiological and environmental factors as the survivors of Dvaraka dispersed worldwide, and how do the named features (-om/-ath/-il aspects, Ta-constant, Galut layers G1-G6) map onto real typological patterns of Indo-Aryan/Dravidian morphology and sound change?
why_now: The Grammatik and Woerterbuch pages - the linguistic core of the site - are the next substantive work under the pending high-priority migration (EXT-ECO-MISH-20260714-001), which will write them from the canonical OTA documents; the README and index page assert that language change is driven by physiological and environmental factors, so the plausibility and educational quality of the site depend on anchoring that claim in documented linguistics rather than asserting it.
validation_summary: The candidate assesses the core Mishkenaz premise (language change through physiological + environmental factors) as supportable in two of three parts: articulatory-perceptual sound change (Ohala) and diaspora/exile language development (koineization, stratification, substrate contact) are well documented — with the Indo-Aryan diaspora (Romani, Domari, Parya, Saurashtra) as the closest real model — while climate-geographic phonology (Everett et al.) is disputed and must not be presented as fact. The named features (-om/-ath/-il, Ta-Konstante, Galut-Layer G1–G6) are not attested forms; only the underlying typological patterns (suffixal aspect morphology, dental -t- perfective marker, real Tamil -il locative, Vedic -tha-, strata model) are real. Since all content pages in this repo are still placeholders and the canonical migration from thomas-kueper.de (EXT-ECO-MISH-20260714-001) is pending, the candidate creates concrete pre-migration verification and enrichment actions for mishkenaz.
